surface_mechanism_description: The ALE growth is controlled by the surface itself, not by the dose of the reactant. Surface saturation is achieved and the desired surface structures are formed via chemisorption reactions.
evidence: In the 1990s the ALE technique was applied to the preparation of catalysts on porous high surface area supports. The primary advantage of ALE is that it allows a good conformal coating. In ALE growth, surface saturation is achieved and the desired surface structures are formed via chemisorption reactions. Therefore ALE growth is controlled by the surface itself, not by the dose of the reactant.
